transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, first of all, I would like to thank the sponsors of this debate and the people of Boston for hosting the debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would like to thank Governor Bush for participating, and I would like to say I’m happy to be here with Tipper and our family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have actually not questioned Governor Bush’s experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have questioned his proposals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And here is why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think this is a very important moment for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have achieved extraordinary prosperity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And in this election, America has to make an important choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Will we use our prosperity to enrich not just the few, but all of our families?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe we have to make the right and responsible choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I’m entrusted with the presidency, here are the choices that I will make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will balance the budget every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will pay down the national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will put Medicare and Social Security in a lockbox and protect them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I will cut taxes for middle-class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe it’s important to resist the temptation to squander our surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If we make the right choices, we can have a prosperity that endures and enriches all of our people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I’m entrusted with the presidency, I will help parents and strengthen families because, you know, if we have prosperity that grows and grows, we still won’t be successful unless we strengthen families by, for example, ensuring that children can always go to schools that are safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: By giving parents the tools to protect their children against cultural pollution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will make sure that we invest in our country and our families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I mean investing in education, health care, the environment, and middle-class tax cuts and retirement security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That is my agenda and that is why I think that it’s not just a question of experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, we do come from different places.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I come from West Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The governor is the chief executive officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We know how to set agendas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think you’ll find the difference reflected in our budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to take one-half of the surplus and dedicate it to Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One-quarter of the surplus for important projects, and I want to send one-quarter of the surplus back to the people who pay the bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want everybody who pays taxes to have their tax rates cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that stands in contrast to my worthy opponent’s plan, which will increase the size of government dramatically.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: His plan is three times larger than President Clinton’s proposed plan eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is a plan that will have 200 new programs — expanded programs and creates 20,000 new bureaucrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It it empowers Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Tonight youâ€™re going to hear that my passion and my vision is to empower Americans to be able to make decisions for themselves in their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yes, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I said that his tax cut plan, for example, raises the question of whether it’s the right choice for the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And let me give you an example of what I mean.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under Governor Bush’s tax cut proposal, he would spend more money on tax cuts for the wealthiest 1% than all of the new spending that he proposes for education, health care, prescription drugs and national defense all combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think those are the wrong priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, under my proposal, for every dollar that I propose in spending for things like education and health care, I will put another dollar into middle class tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And for every dollar that I spend in those two categories, I’ll put $2 toward paying down the national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s very important to keep the debt going down and completely eliminate it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I also think it’s very important to go to the next stage of welfare reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Our country has cut the welfare rolls in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I fought hard from my days in the Senate and as vice president to cut the welfare rolls and we’ve moved millions of people in America into good jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it’s now time for the next stage of welfare reform, and include fathers and not only mothers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me just say that obviously tonight we’re going to hear some phony numbers about what I think and what we ought to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People need to know that over the next ten years it is going to be $25 trillion of revenue that comes into our treasurey and we anticipate spending $21 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And my plan say why don’t we pass 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 3 trillion of that back to the people who pay the bills?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surely we can afford 5% of the $25 trillion that are coming into the treasury to the hard working people that pay the bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent thinks the government — the surplus is the government’s money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what I think.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s the hard-working people of America’s money and I want to share some of that money with you so you have more money to build and save and dream for your families.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a difference between government making decisions for you and you getting more of your money to make decisions for yourself.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I take him for his word.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look, I fully recognize I’m not of Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m from Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he’s got a lot of experience, but so do I.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been the chief executive officer of the second biggest state in the union.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have a proud record of working with both Republicans and Democrats, which is what our nation needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Somebody that can come to Washington and say let’s forget all the finger pointing and get positive things done on Medicare, prescription drugs, Social Security, and so I take him for his word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Jim, if I could just respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor used the phrase phony numbers, but if you look at the plan and add the numbers up, these numbers are correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He spends more money for tax cuts for the wealthiest 1% than all of his new spending proposals for health care, prescription drugs, education and national defense all combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I agree that the surplus is the American people’s money, it’s your money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I don’t think we should give nearly half of it to the wealthiest 1%, because the other 99% have had an awful lot to do with building the surplus in our prosperity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope itâ€™s about wealthy people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Actually what I’ve said, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve said that eight years ago they campaigned on prescription drugs for seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And four years ago they campaigned on getting prescription drugs for seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now they’re campaigning on getting prescription drugs for seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It seems like they can’t get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, they may blame other folks, but it’s time to get somebody in Washington who is going to work with both Republicans and Democrats to get some positive things done when it comes to our seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so what I’ve said is that there’s been some missed opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’ve had a chance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’ve had a chance to form consensus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a plan on Medicare, for example, that’s a two-stage plan that says we’ll have immediate help for seniors and what I call immediate Helping Hand, a $48 billion program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I also want to say to seniors, if you’re happy with Medicare the way it is, fine, you can stay in the program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’re going to give you additional choices like they give federal employees in the federal employee health plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They have a variety of choices to choose, so should seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And my point has been, as opposed to politicizing an issue like Medicare, in other words, holding it up as an issue, hoping somebody bites it and try to clobber them over the head with it for political purposes, this year, in the year 2000, it’s time to get it done once and for all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’ve been critical about the administration for.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Same with Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think there was a good opportunity to bring Republicans and Democrats together to reform the Social Security system so seniors will never go without.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Those on Social Security today will have their promise made, but also to give younger workers the option at their choice of being able to manage some of their own money in the private sector to make sure there’s a Social Security system around tomorrow.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are a lot of young workers at our rallies we go to that when they hear I’ll trust them at their option to be able to manage, under certain guidelines, some of their own money to get a better rate of return so that they’ll have a retirement plan in the future, they begin to nod their heads and they want a different attitude in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, under my plan all seniors will get prescription drugs under Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor has described Medicare as a government HMO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s not, and let me explain the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under the Medicare prescription drug proposal I’m making, here is how it works, you go to your own doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Your doctor chooses your prescription.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: No HMO or insurance company can take those choices away from you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Then you go to your own pharmacy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You fill the prescription and Medicare pays half the cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you’re in a very poor family or if you have very high costs, Medicare will pay all the costs, a $25 premium, and much better benefits than you can possibly find in the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now here is the contrast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 95% of all seniors would get no help whatsoever under my opponent’s plan for the first four or five years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, one thing I don’t understand, Jim, is why is it that the wealthiest 1% get their tax cuts the first year, but 95% of seniors have to wait four to five years before they get a single penny?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I guess my answer to that is the man is running on Medi-scare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Trying to frighten people in the voting booth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s just not the way I think and it’s not my intentions and not my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want all seniors to have prescription drugs in Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to reform Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thereâ€™s been opportunity to do so but this administration has failed to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so seniors will have not only a Medicare plan where the poor seniors will have prescription drugs paid for, but there will be a variety of options.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The current system today has meant a lot for a lot of seniors, and I really appreciate the intentions of the current system as I mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re happy with the system you can stay in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there are a lot of procedures that haven’t kept up in Medicare with the current times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No prescription drug benefits, no drug therapy, no preventative medicines, no vision care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to have a modern system to help seniors, and the idea of supporting a federally controlled 132,000-page document bureaucracy as being a compassionate way for seniors, and the only compassionate source of care for seniors is not my vision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we ought to give seniors more options.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we ought to make the system work better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know it will require a different kind of leader to go to Washington to say to both Republicans and Democrats, let’s come together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve had your chance, Vice President, you’ve been there for eight years and nothing has been done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My point is, is that my plan not only trusts seniors with options, my plan sets aside $3.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 4 trillion for Medicare over the next ten years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My plan also says it requires a new approach in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to require somebody who can work across the partisan divide.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I could respond to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan I will put Medicare in an iron clad lockbox and prevent the money from being used for anything other than Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor has declined to endorse that idea even though the Republican as well as Democratic leaders in Congress have endorsed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would be interested to see if he would say this evening he’ll put Medicare in a lockbox.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I donâ€™t think he will because under his plan if you work out the numbers Â $100 billion comes out of Medicare just for the wealthiest 1% in the tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now here is the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Some people who say the word reform actually mean cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under the governor’s plan, if you kept the same fee for service that you have now under Medicare, your premiums would go up by between 18% and 47%, and that is the study of the Congressional plan that he’s modeled his proposal on by the Medicare actuaries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you one quick example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There is a man here tonight named George McKinney from Milwaukee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He’s 70 years old, has high blood pressure, his wife has heart trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They have an income of $25,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They can’t pay for their prescription drugs and so they’re some of the ones that go to Canada regularly in order to get their prescription drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan, half of their costs would be paid right away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under Governor Bush’s plan, they would get not one penny for four to five years and then they would be forced to go into an HMO or to an insurance company and ask them for coverage, but there would be no limit on the premiums or the deductibles or any of the terms and conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I cannot let this go by, the old-style Washington politics, of we’re going to scare you in the voting booth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan the man gets immediate help with prescription drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s called Immediate Helping Hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Instead of squabbling and finger pointing, he gets immediate help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me say something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Can I make another point?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They get $25,000 a year income, that makes them ineligible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look, this is a man who has great numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talks about numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m beginning to think not only did he invent the Internet, but he invented the calculator.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s fuzzy math.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a scaring — he’s trying to scare people in the voting booth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Under my tax plan that he continues to criticize, I set one-third.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The federal government should take no more than a third of anybody’s check.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I also dropped the bottom rate from 15% to 10%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because by far the vast majority of the help goes to people at the bottom end of the economic ladder.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a family of four in Massachusetts, making $50,000, you get a 50% cut in the federal income taxes you pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s from $4000 to about $2000.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, the difference in our plans is I want that $2,000 to go to you, and the vice president would like to be spending the $2,000 on your behalf.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s just clear you can go to the website and look.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you make more than $25,000 a year you don’t get a penny of help under the Bush prescription drug proposal for at least four to five years, and then you’re pushed into a Medicare — into an HMO or insurance company plan, and there’s no limit on the premiums or the deductibles or any of the conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the insurance companies say it won’t work and they won’t offer these plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The difference is I want to bring it to 100% and he wants to bring it to 5%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s totally false for him to stand up here and say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me make sure the seniors hear me loud and clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They have had their chance to get something done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to work with Democrats and Republicans to reform the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All seniors will be covered, all poor seniors will have their prescription drugs paid for, and in the meantime, we’ll have a plan to help poor seniors and in the meantime it could be one year or two years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me call your attention to the key word there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He said all poor seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All seniors are covered under prescription drugs in my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the first year?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we can get it done in the first year, you bet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yours is phased in in eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s a two-phase plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: For the first four years — it takes a year to pass it and for the first four years only the poor are covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Middle class seniors like George McKinney and his wife are not covered for four to five years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Excellent question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And here is the simple difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My plan has not only a short-term component, but also a long-term component.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And it focuses not only on increasing the supply, which I think we have to do, but also on working on the consumption side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, in the short-term we have to free ourselves from the domination of the big oil companies that have the ability to manipulate the price from OPEC when they want to raise the price.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And in the long-term we have to give new incentives for the development of domestic resources like deep gas in the western Gulf, like stripper wells for oil, but also renewable sources of energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And domestic sources that are cleaner and better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’m proposing a plan that will give tax credits and tax incentives for the rapid development of new kinds of cars and trucks and buses and factories and boilers and furnaces that don’t have as much pollution, that don’t burn as much energy, and that help us get out on the cutting edge of the new technologies that will create millions of new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because, when we sell these new products here, we’ll then be able to sell them overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There is a ravenous demand for them overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, another big difference is Governor Bush is proposing to open up some of our most precious environmental treasures, like the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge for the big oil companies to go in and start producing oil there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that is the wrong choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It would only give us a few months’ worth of oil and the oil wouldn’t start flowing for many years into the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s a fair price to pay to destroy precious parts of America’s environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to bet on the future and move beyond the current technologies to have a whole new generation of more efficient, cleaner, energy technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an issue I know a lot about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was a small oil person for a while in west Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is an administration that’s had no plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And all of a sudden the results of having no plan have caught up with America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First and foremost we have to fully fund LIHEAP which is a way to help low income folks, particularly here in the east to pay for high fuel bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we need an active exploration program in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The only way to become less dependent on foreign sources of crude oil is to explore at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You bet I want to open up a small part of Alaska.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When that field is online it will produce one million barrels a day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Today we import one million barrels from Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would rather that a million come from our own hemisphere, our own country as opposed to Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to build more pipelines to move natural gas throughout this hemisphere.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to develop the coal resources in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Have clean coal technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Weâ€™ve got abundant supplies of energy here in America and weâ€™d better get after it, we better start exploring it or otherwise we’ll be in deep trouble in the future because of our dependency upon foreign sources of crude.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me clarify.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m for doing something both on the supply side and production side and on the consumption side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me say, that I found one thing in Governor Bush’s answer that we certainly agree on, and that’s the low income heating assistance program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I commend you for supporting that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I worked to get $400 million just a couple of weeks ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And to establish a permanent home heating oil reserve here in the northeast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, as for the proposals that I’ve worked for for renewables and conservation and efficiencies and new technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The fact is for the last few years in the Congress, we’ve faced a lot of opposition to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’ve only approved about 10% of the agenda I’ve helped to send up there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to get serious about this energy crisis, both in the Congress and in the White House, and if you entrust me with the presidency, I will tackle this problem and focus on new technologies that will make us less dependent on big oil or foreign oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well I would first say he should have been tackling it for the last seven years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly the difference is we need to explore at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the vice president doesn’t believe in exploration in Alaska.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a lot of shut-in gas that we need to be moving out of Alaska by pipeline.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s an interesting issue up in the northwest as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Do we remove dams that produce hydroelectric energy?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m against removing dams in the northwest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I donâ€™t know where the vice president stands but thatâ€™s a renewable energy source of energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to keep that in line.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was in coal country in West Virginia yesterday.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is an abundant supply of coal in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know we can do a better job of clean coal technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to ask the Congress for $2 billion to make sure we have the cleanest coal technologies in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My answer to you is in the short-term we need to get after it here in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to explore our resources and we need to develop our reservoirs of domestic production.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We also need to have a hemispheric energy policy where Canada, Mexico and the United States come together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I brought this up recently with Vincent Fox the newly elected president in Mexico, he’s a man I know from Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I talked to him about how best to expedite the exploration of natural gas in Mexico and transport it up to the United States so we become less dependent on foreign sources of crude oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a major problem facing America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The administration did not deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a new administration to deal with the energy problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I may just briefly, Jim, note.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I found a couple of other things we agree upon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We may not find that many this evening, so I wanted to emphasize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I strongly support new investments in clean coal technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I made a proposal three months ago on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And also domestic exploration yes, but not in the environmental treasures of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s the wrong choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know the oil companies have been itching to do that, but it is not the right thing for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the right thing for the consumers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Less dependency upon foreign sources of crude is good for consumers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we can do so in an environmentally friendly way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well can I have the last word on this?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think a president can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was disappointed in the ruling because I think abortions ought to be more rare in America, and I’m worried that that pill will create more abortions and cause more people to have abortions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a very important topic and it’s a very sensitive topic, because a lot of good people disagree on the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think what the next president ought to do is to promote a culture of life in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Life of the elderly and life of those living all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Life of the unborn.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, I think a noble goal for this country is that every child, born or unborn, need to be protected by law and welcomed to life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know we need to change a lot of minds before we get there in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I do believe is that we can find good, common ground on issues of parental consent or parental notification.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know we need to ban partial birth abortions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a place where my opponent and I have strong disagreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe banning partial birth abortions would be a positive step to reducing the number of abortions in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is an issue that will require a new attitude.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been battling over abortion for a long period of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surely this nation can come together to promote the value of life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surely we can fight off these laws that will encourage doctors to — to allow doctors to take the lives of our seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surely we can work together to create a cultural life so some of these youngsters who feel like they can take a neighbor’s life with a gun will understand that that’s not the way America is meant to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surely we can find common ground to reduce the number of abortions in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As to the drug itself, I mentioned I was disappointed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope the FDA took its time to make sure that American women will be safe who use this drug.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, the FDA took 12 years, and I do support that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They determined it was medically safe for the women who use that drug.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This is indeed a very important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: First of all on the issue of partial birth or so-called late-term abortion, I would sign a law banning that procedure, provided that doctors have the ability to save a woman’s life or to act if her health is severely at risk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the main issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The main issue is whether or not the Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Wade decision is going to be overturned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I support a woman’s right to choose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My opponent does not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is important because the next president is going to appoint three and maybe even four justices of the Supreme Court.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And Governor Bush has declared to the anti-choice groups that he will appoint justices in the mold of Scalia and Clarence Thomas, who are known for being the most vigorous opponents of a woman’s right to choose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here is the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He trusts the government to order a woman to do what it thinks she ought to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I trust women to make the decisions that affect their lives, their destinies and their bodies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think a woman’s right to choose ought to be protected and defended.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think a president can unilaterally overturn it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The FDA has made its decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think once a decision has been made, it’s been made unless it’s proven to be unsafe to women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Jim, the question you asked, if I heard you correctly, was would he support legislation to overturn it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And if I heard the statement day before yesterday, you said you would order — he said he would order his FDA appointee to review the decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now that sounds to me a little bit different.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I just think that we ought to support the decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I said I would make sure that women would be safe who used the drug.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am pro-life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The voters should assume I have no litmus test on that issue or any other issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Voters will know I’ll put competent judges on the bench.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People who will strictly interpret the Constitution and not use the bench to write social policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is going to be a big difference between my opponent and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that the judges ought not to take the place of the legislative branch of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That they’re appointed for life and that they ought to look at the Constitution as sacred.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They shouldn’t misuse their bench.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe in liberal activist judges.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe in strict constructionists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Those are the kind of judges I will appoint.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve named four supreme court justices in the State of Texas and would ask the people to check out their qualifications, their deliberations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re good, solid men and women who have made good, sound judgments on behalf of the people of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We both use similar language to reach an exactly opposite outcome.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t favor a litmus test, but I know that there are ways to assess how a potential justice interprets the Constitution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And in my view, the Constitution ought to be interpreted as a document that grows with our country and our history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I believe, for example, that there is a right of privacy in the Fourth Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And when the phrase a strict constructionist is used and when the names of Scalia and Thomas are used as the benchmarks for who would be appointed, those are code words, and nobody should mistake this, for saying the governor would appoint people who would overturn Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Wade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s very clear to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would appoint people that have a philosophy that I think would have it quite likely they would uphold Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Wade.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It sounds like the vice presidentâ€™s not right very many times tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just told you the criteria on which I’ll appoint judges.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have a record of appointing judges in the State of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what a governor gets to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A governor gets to name supreme court judges.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He also reads all kinds of things into my tax plan and into my Medicare plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want the viewers out there to listen to what I have to say about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It would be likely that they would uphold Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Wade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I do believe it’s wrong to use a litmus test.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you look at the history of a lower court judge’s rulings, you can get a pretty good idea of how they’ll interpret questions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: A lot of questions are first impression, and these questions that have been seen many times come up in a new context and so — but, you know, this is a very important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because a lot of young women in this country take this right for granted and it could be lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is on the ballot in this election, make no mistake about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you what kind of judges he’ll put on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’ll put liberal activists justices who will use their bench to subvert the legislature, that’s what he’ll do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Thatâ€™s not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, Milosevic has lost the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: His opponent, Kostunica, has won the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s overwhelming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Milosevic’s government refuses to release the vote count.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There’s now a general strike going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’re demonstrating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we should support the people of Serbia and Yugoslavia, as they call the Serbia plus Montenegro, and put pressure in every way possible to recognize the lawful outcome of the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The people of Serbia have acted very bravely in kicking this guy out of office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now he is trying to not release the votes and then go straight to a so-called runoff election without even announcing the results of the first vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’ve made it clear, along with our allies, that when Milosevic leaves, then Serbia will be able to have a more normal relationship with the rest of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That is a very strong incentive that we’ve given them to do the right thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Bear in mind also, Milosevic has been indicted as a war criminal and he should be held accountable for his actions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have to take measured steps because the sentiment within Serbia is, for understandable reasons, against the United States because their nationalism — even if they don’t like Milosevic, they still have some feelings lingering from the NATO action there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So we have to be intelligent in the way we go about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But make no mistake about it, we should do everything we can to see that the will of the Serbian people expressed in this extraordinary election is done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I hope that he’ll be out of office very shortly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m pleased with the results of the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As the vice president is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for the man to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It means that the United States must have a strong diplomatic hand with our friends in NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why it’s important to make sure our alliances are as strong as they possibly can be to keep the pressure on Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Milosevic.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But this will be an interesting moment for the Russians to step up and lead as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Be a wonderful time for the Russians to step into the Balkans and convince Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Milosevic that it’s in his best interest and his country’s best interest to leave office.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Russians have a lot of sway in that part of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We would like to see the Russians use that sway to encourage democracy to take hold.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an encouraging election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for the man to leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In this particular situation, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Bear in mind that we have a lot of sanctions in force against Serbia right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the people of Serbia know that they can escape all those sanctions if this guy is turned out of power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I understand what the governor has said about asking the Russians to be involved, and under some circumstances that might be a good idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But being as they have not yet been willing to recognize Kostunica as the lawful winner of the election, I’m not sure it’s right for us to invite the president of Russia to mediate this — this dispute there because we might not like the results that comes out of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They currently favor going forward with a runoff election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s the wrong thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think the governor’s instinct is not necessarily bad because we have worked with the Russians in a constructive way in Kosovo, for example, to end the conflict there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I think we need to be very careful in the present situation before we invite the Russians to play the lead role in mediating.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well obviously we wouldn’t use the Russians if they didn’t agree with our answer, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They donâ€™t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me say this to you, I wouldn’t use force.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t use force.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not in our national interest to use force in this case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would use pressure and diplomacy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a difference with what the president did in Kosovo which I supported and this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s up to the people in this region to take control of their country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, if it’s in our vital national interests, and that means whether our territory is threatened or people could be harmed, whether or not the alliances are — our defense alliances are threatened, whether or not our friends in the Middle East are threatened.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That would be a time to seriously consider the use of force.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, whether or not the mission was clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Whether or not it was a clear understanding as to what the mission would be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thirdly, whether or not we were prepared and trained to win.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Whether or not our forces were of high morale and high standing and well-equipped.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And finally, whether or not there was an exit strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would take the use of force very seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would be guarded in my approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we can be all things to all people in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve got to be very careful when we commit our troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The vice president and I have a disagreement about the use of troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He believes in nation building.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would be very careful about using our troops as nation builders.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe the role of the military is to fight and win war and therefore prevent war from happening in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I would take my responsibility seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it starts with making sure we rebuild our military power.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Morale in today’s military is too low.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re having trouble meeting recruiting goals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We met the goals this year, but in the previous years we have not met recruiting goals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some of our troops are not well-equipped.
