transcript_turns.text: He has a 15-year-old daughter named Caley, who is in Sarasota High School.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Her science class was supposed to be for 24 students.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She’s the 36th student in that classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They sent me a picture of her in the classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They can’t squeeze another desk in for her, so she has to stand during class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want the federal government, consistent with local control and new accountability, to make improvement of our schools the number one priority so Caley will have a desk and can sit down in a classroom where she can learn.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The first is, the difference is there is no new accountability measures in Vice President Gore’s plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He says he’s for voluntary testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have voluntary testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You must have mandatory testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You must say that if you receive money you must show us whether or not children are learning to read and write and add and subtract.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You may claim you’ve got mandatory testing but you don’t, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a huge difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Testing is the cornerstone of reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know how I know?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because it’s the cornerstone of reform in the State of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Republicans and Democrats came together and said what can we do to make our public education the best in the country?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done a long way working together to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The cornerstone is to have strong accountability in return for money and in return for flexibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to ask you to show us whether or not — we ask you to post the results on the Internet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We encourage parents to take a look at the comparative results of schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a strong charter school movement that I signed the legislation to get started in the State of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe if we find poor children trapped in schools that won’t teach, we need to free the parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to expand education savings accounts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Something that the vice presidentâ€™s running mate supports.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s big differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He won’t support freeing local districts from the strings of federal money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I do have mandatory testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think the governor may not have heard what I said clearly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The voluntary national testing is in addition to the mandatory testing that we require of states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: All schools, all school districts, students themselves, and required teacher testing, which goes a step farther than Governor Bush has been willing to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here are a couple of differences, though, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Governor Bush is in favor of vouchers which take taxpayer money away from public schools and give them to private schools that are not accountable for how the money is used and don’t have to take all applicants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, private schools play a great role in our society.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: All of our children have gone to both public schools and private schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think private schools should have a right to take taxpayer money away from public schools at a time when Caley Ellis is standing in that classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you another example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I went to a school in Dade County, Florida where the facilities are so overcrowded the children have to eat lunch in shifts with the first shift for lunch starting at 9:30 in the morning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, this is a funding crisis all around the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There are fewer parents of school-age children as a percentage of the voting population and there is the largest generation of students ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’re in an information age when learning is more important than ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 90% of our kids go to public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to make it the number one priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Modernize our schools, reduce class size, recruit new teachers, give every child a chance to learn with one-on-one time in a quality — high-quality, safe school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If it’s a failing school, shut it down and reopen it under a new principal with a turnaround team of specialists the way Governor Jim Hunt does in North Carolina.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here is another difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor, if it’s a failing school, would leave the children in that failing school for three years and then give a little bit of money to the parents, a down payment on a down payment for private school tuition, and pretend that that would be enough for them to go out and go to a private school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s an illusion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, most of good governance is at the state level.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See, here is the mentality.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to make the state do this and make the state do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All I’m saying is if you spend money, show us results and test every year, which you do not do, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You don’t test every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can say you do to the cameras but you don’t, unless you’ve changed your plan here on the stage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You need to test every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s how you determine if children are progressing to excellence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, one of the things that we have to be careful about in politics is throwing money at a system that has not yet been reformed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: More money is needed and I spend more money, but step one is to make sure we reform the system to have the system in place that leaves no child behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Stop this business about asking gosh, how old are you?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re 10 we’ll put you here, 12 you put here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Start asking the question, what do you know?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t know what you’re supposed to know, we’ll make sure you do early before it’s too late.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When the action in Kosovo was dragging on and we were searching for a solution to the problem, our country had defeated the adversary on the battlefield without a single American life being lost in combat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But the dictator Milosevic was hanging on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I invited the former prime minister of Russia to my house and took a risk in asking him to get personally involved, along with the head of Finland, to go to Belgrade and to take a set of proposals from the United States that would constitute basically a surrender by Serbia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it was a calculated risk that paid off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I could probably give you some other examples of decisions over the last 24 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have been in public service for 24 years, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And throughout all that time the people I have fought for have been the middle-class families, and I have been willing to stand up to powerful interests like the big insurance companies, the drug companies, the HMOs, the oil companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They have good people and they play constructive roles sometimes, but sometimes they get too much power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I cast my lot with the people even when it means that you have to stand up to some powerful interests who are trying to turn the — the policies and the laws to their advantage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You can see it in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The big drug companies support Governor Bush’s prescription drug proposal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They oppose mine because they don’t want to get Medicare involved because they’re afraid that Medicare will negotiate lower prices for seniors who currently pay the highest prices of all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been standing up to big Hollywood, big trial lawyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Was â€“ what was the question?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was about emergencies, wasn’t it?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, as governor, one of the things you have to deal with is catastrophe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can remember the fires that swept Parker County, Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember the floods that swept our state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember going down to Del Rio, Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have to pay the administration a compliment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: James Lee Witt of FEMA has done a really good job of working with governors during times of crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But that’s the time when you’re tested not only — it’s the time to test your mettle, a time to test your heart when you see people whose lives have been turned upside down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It broke my heart to go to the flood scene in Del Rio where a fellow and his family got completely uprooted.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The only thing I knew to do was to get aid as quickly as possible with state and federal help, and to put my arms around the man and his family and cry with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what governors do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They are often on the front line of catastrophic situations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, it depends, obviously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But what I would do first and foremost, is I would get in touch with the Federal Reserve Chairman, Alan Greenspan, to find out all the facts and all the circumstances.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would have my Secretary of the Treasury be in touch with the financial centers not only here, but at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would make sure that key members of Congress were called in to discuss the gravity of the situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I would come up with a game plan to deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what governors end up doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We end up being problem solvers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We come up with practical, common sense solutions for problems that we’re confronted with.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In this case, in the case of a financial crisis, I would gather all the facts before I made the decision as to what the government ought or ought not to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: First I want to compliment the governor on his response to those fires and floods in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I accompanied James Lee Witt down to Texas when those fires broke out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And FEMA has been a major flagship project of our reinventing government efforts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I agree, it works extremely well now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: On the international financial crises that come up, my friend, Bob Rubin, the former Secretary of Treasury is here, he’s a close advisor to me and great friend in all respects.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have had a chance to work with him and Alan Greenspan and others on the crisis following the collapse of the Mexican peso.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When the Asian financial crisis raised the risk of world-wide recession that could affect our economy, And now, of course, the euro’s value has been dropping, but seems to be under control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it started for me in the last eight years when I had the honor of casting the tie-breaking vote to end the old economic plan here at home and put into place a new economic plan that has helped us to make some progress, 22 million new jobs, the greatest prosperity ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not good enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My attitude is you ain’t seen nothing yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We need to do more and better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, there’s no difference on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a difference, though, as to what the economy has meant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the economy has meant more for the Gore and Clinton folks than the Gore and Clinton folks have meant for the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think most of the economic growth that has taken place is a result of ingenuity and hard work and entrepreneurship and that’s the role of goverment to encourage that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of in response to the question, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Can I comment on that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know, I think the American people deserve credit for the great economy that we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s their ingenuity, I agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But you know, they were working pretty hard eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And now they had ingenuity eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The difference is we’ve got a new policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And instead of concentrating on tax cuts mostly for the wealthy, we want — I want tax cuts for the middle-class families and I want to continue the prosperity and make sure that it enriches not just a few but all of our families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have gone from the biggest deficits to the biggest surpluses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have gone from a triple-dip recession during the previous 12 years to a tripling of the stock market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Instead of a high unemployment, we have the lowest African-American and Latin American unemployment rates in history and 22 million new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s not good enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Too many people have been left behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have got to do much more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The key is job training, education, investments in health care and education, environment, retirement security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And incidentally, we have got to preserve Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m totally opposed to diverting one out of every six dollars out of the Social Security trust fund, as the Governor has proposed, into the stock market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want new incentives for savings and investment for the young couples who are working hard so they can save and invest on their own on top of Social Security, not at the expense of Social Security, as the governor proposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Two points.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One, a lot of folks are still waiting for that 1992 middle-class tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember the vice president saying, “Just give us a chance to get up there, we’re going to make sure you get tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” It didn’t happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now he’s having to say that again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’ve had their chance to deliver a tax cut to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, the surest way to bust this economy is to increase the role and size of the federal budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Senate Budget Committee did a study of the vice president’s expenditures.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s been projected that they could conceivably bust the budget by $900 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That means he’ll either have to raise your taxes by $900 billion or go into the Social Security surplus for $900 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a plan that is going to increase the bureaucracy by 20,000 people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: His targeted tax cut is so detailed, so much fine print that it is going to require numerous IRS agents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need somebody to simplify the code, to be fair, to continue prosperity by sharing some of the surplus with the people who pay the bills, particularly those at the bottom end of the economic ladder.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I could respond, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: What he’s quoting is not the Senate Budget Commiitte, it is a partisan press release by the Republicans on the Senate Budget Committee that’s not worth the government — the taxpayer-paid paper that it’s printed on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, as for 20,000 new bureaucrats, as you call them, you know, the size of the federal government will go down in a Gore administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the reinventing government program you just look at the numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is 300,000 people smaller today than it was eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, the fact is you’re going to have a hard time convincing folks that we were a whole lot better off eight years ago than we are today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But that’s not the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The question is, will we be better off four years from now than we are today?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And as for the surest way to threaten our prosperity, having a $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 9 trillion tax cut, almost half of which goes to the wealthy, and a $1 trillion Social Security privatization proposal is the surest way to put our budget into deficit â€“ raise interest rates and put our prosperity at risk.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t let the man continue with fuzzy math.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 3 trillion Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will go to everybody who pays taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to be the kind of president that says you get tax relief and you don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to be a picker and chooser.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What is fair is everybody who pays taxes ought to get relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Suits me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I do disagree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because if we can keep our prosperity going, if we can continue balancing the budget and paying down the debt, then the strong economy keeps generating surpluses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here is my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will keep Social Security in a lockbox and that pays down the national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the interest savings I would put right back into Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That extends the life of Social Security for 55 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think that it’s very important to understand that cutting benefits under Social Security means that people like Winifred Skinner from Des Moines, Iowa, who is here, would really have a much harder time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because there are millions of seniors who are living almost hand to mouth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And you talk about cutting benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t go along with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I am opposed to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m also opposed to a plan that diverts 1 out of every $6 away from the Social Security Trust Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Social Security is a trust fund that pays the checks this year with the money that is paid into Social Security this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor wants to divert 1 out of every $6 off into the stock market, which means that he would drain a trillion dollars out of the Social Security Trust Fund in this generation over the next ten years, and Social Security under that approach would go bankrupt within this generation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: His leading advisor on this plan actually said that would be okay, because then the Social Security Trust Fund could start borrowing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It would borrow up to $3 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, Social Security has never done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think it should do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it should stay in a lockbox, and I’ll tell you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will veto anything that takes money out of Social Security for privatization or anything else other than Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought it was interesting that on the two minutes he spent about a million-and-a-half on my plan, which means he doesn’t want you to know what he’s doing is loading up IOUs for future generations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He puts no real assets into the Social Security system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The revenues exceed the expenses in Social Security until the year 2015 which means all retirees are going to get the promises made.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For those of you who he wants to scare into the voting booth to vote for him, hear me loud and clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A promise made will be a promise kept.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You bet we want to allow younger workers to take some of their own money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The vice president thinks it’s the government’s money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The payroll taxes are your money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You ought to put it in prudent, safe investments so that $1 trillion over the next ten years grows to be $3 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The money stays within the Social Security system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a part of the Social Security system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He claims it will be out of Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s your money, it’s a part of your retirement benefit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a fundamental difference between what we believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want you to have your own asset that you can call your own.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That you can pass on from one generation to the next.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to get a better rate of return for your own money than the paltry 2% that the current Social Security Trust gets today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Greenspan I thought missed an opportunity to say there’s a third way, and that is to get a better rate of return on the Social Security monies coming into the trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 3 trillion of surplus that we can use to make sure that younger workers have a Social Security plan in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we’re smart and if we trust workers and if we understand the power of the compounding rate of interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here is the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I give a new incentive for younger workers to save their own money and invest their own money, but not at the expense of Social Security, on top of Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My plan is Social Security plus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor’s plan is Social Security minus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Your future benefits would be cut by the amount that’s diverted into the stock market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you make bad investments, that’s too bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But even before then the problem hits because the money contributed to Social Security this year is an entitlement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s how it works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the money is used to pay the benefits for seniors this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you cut the amount going in 1 out of every $6, then you have to cut the value of each check by 1 out of every $6 unless you come up with the money from somewhere else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would like to know from the governor — I know we’re not supposed to ask each other questions — but I’d be interested in knowing, does that trillion dollars come from the trust fund, or does it come from the rest of the budget?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s enough money to pay seniors today in the current affairs of Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The trillion comes from the surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Surplus is money — more money than needed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you what your plan is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not Social Security plus, it’s Social Security plus huge debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is what it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You leave future generations with tremendous IOUs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to have a leader that doesn’t put off tomorrow what we should do today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to have somebody to step up and say look, let’s let younger workers take some of their own money and under certain guidelines invest it in the private markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The safest of federal investments yields 4%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s twice the amount of rate of return than the current Social Security Trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a fundamental difference of opinion here, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Younger worker after younger worker hears my call that says I trust you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you know what, the issue is changing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Seniors now understand that the promise made will be a promise kept, but younger workers now understand we better have a government that trusts them and that’s exactly what I’m going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Could I respond to that, Jim?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This is a big issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Could we do another round on it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Just briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When FDR established Social Security, they didn’t call them IOUs, they called it the full faith and credit of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t have trust in that, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you take it out of the surplus in the trust fund, that means the trust fund goes bankrupt in this generation within 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a government that thinks a 2% rate of return on your money is satisfactory.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a government that says younger workers can’t possibly have their own assets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to think differently about the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to make sure our seniors get the promise made.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t trust younger workers to manage some of their own money with the Social Security surplus, to grow from $1 trillion to $3 trillion, it will be impossible to bridge the gap without it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Gore’s plan will do causing huge payroll taxes or major benefit reductions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The man loves his wife and I appreciate that a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I love mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The man loves his family a lot, and I appreciate that, because I love my family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the thing that discouraged me about the vice president was uttering those famous words, “No controlling legal authority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” I felt like there needed to be a better sense of responsibility of what was going on in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that — I believe they’ve moved that sign, “The buck stops here” from the Oval Office desk to “The buck stops here” on the Lincoln bedroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not good for the country and it’s not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to have a new look about how we conduct ourselves in office.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a huge trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see it all the time when people come up to me and say, I don’t want you to let me down again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we can do better than the past administration has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a fresh start.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a new look.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a fresh start after a season of cynicism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I don’t know the man well, but I’ve been disappointed about how he and his administration have conducted the fundraising affairs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, going to a Buddhist temple and then claiming it wasn’t a fundraiser isn’t my view of responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to attack our country’s problems, not attack each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to spend my time making this country even better than it is, not trying to make you out to be a bad person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You may want to focus on scandal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to focus on results.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: As I said a couple of months ago, I stand here as my own man and I want you to see me for who I really am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Tipper and I have been married for 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We became grandparents a year-and-a-half ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got four children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have devoted 24 years of my life to public service and I’ve said this before and I’ll say it again, if you entrust me with the presidency, I may not be the most exciting politician, but I will work hard for you every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will fight for middle-class families and working men and women and I will never let you down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They ought to factor in it when they go to the voting booth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think people need to be held responsible for the actions they take in life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that — well, I think that’s part of the need for a cultural change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to say we each need to be responsible for what we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People in the highest office of the land must be responsible for decisions they make in life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the way I’ve conducted myself as Governor of Texas and that’s the way I’ll conduct myself as President of the United States, should I be fortunate enough to earn your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people should take into account who we are as individuals, what our experience is, what our positions are on the issues and proposals are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m asking you to see me for who I really am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m offering you my own vision, my own experience, my own proposals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And incidentally, one of them is this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This current campaign financing system has not reflected credit on anybody in either party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that’s one of the reasons I’ve said before, and I’ll pledge here tonight, if I’m president, the very first bill that Joe Lieberman and I will send to the United States Congress is the McCain-Feingold campaign finance reform bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the reason it’s that important is that all of the other issues, whether prescription drugs for all seniors that are opposed by the drug companies or the patient’s bill of rights to take the decisions away from the HMOs and give them to the doctors and nurses, opposed by the HMOs and insurance companies, all these other proposals are going to be a lot easier to get passed for the American people if we limit the influence of special interest money and give democracy back to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I wish Governor Bush would join me this evening in endorsing the McCain-Feingold Campaign Finance Reform Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, this man has no credibility on the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, I read in the “New York Times” where he said he co-sponsored the McCain-Feingold Campaign Fundraising Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he wasn’t in the Senate with Senator Feingold.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so, look, I’m going to — what you need to know about me is I will uphold the law, I’m going to have an attorney general that enforces the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The time for campaign funding reform is after the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This man has outspent me and the special interests are outspending me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I am not going to lay down my arms in the middle of the campaign for somebody who has got no credibility on the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would support an effort to ban corporate soft money and labor union soft money so long as there was dues check-off.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve campaigned on this since the primaries.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe there needs to be instant disclosure on the Internet as to who has given to who.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to fully enforce the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to have an attorney general that says if a law is broken, we’ll enforce it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Be strict and firm about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, Governor Bush, you have attacked my character and credibility and I am not going to respond in kind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to focus on the problems and not attack each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One of the serious problems, hear me well, is that our system of government is being undermined by too much influence coming from special interest money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to get a handle on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And like John McCain, I have learned from experience, and it’s not a new position for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 24 years ago I supported full public financing of all federal elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And anybody who thinks I’m just saying it, it will be the first bill I send to the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want you to know I care passionately about this and I will fight until it becomes law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want people to hear what he just said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is for full public financing of Congressional elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m absolutely, adamently opposed to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want the government financing congressional elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank the University of Massachusetts and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It has been a good, lively exchange.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a huge difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mine is I want to empower people in their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I also want to go to Washington to get some positive things done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is going to require a new spirit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A spirit of cooperation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will require the ability of a Republican president to reach out across the partisan divide and to say to Democrats, let’s come together to do what is right for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s been my record as Governor of Texas, it will be how I conduct myself if I’m fortunate enough to earn your vote as President of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to finally get something done on Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure prescription drugs are available for all seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I want seniors to have additional choices when it comes to choosing their health care plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to finally get something done on Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure the seniors have the promise made will be a promise kept, but I want younger workers to be able to manage some of their own money, some of their own payroll taxes in the private sector under certain guidelines to get a better rate of return on your own money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to rebuild our military to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to have a strong hand when it comes to the United States in world affairs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to try to put our troops in all places at all times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to be the world’s policeman, I want to be the world’s peacemaker by having a military of high morale and a military that is well-equipped.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want anti-ballistic missile systems to protect ourselves and our allies from a rogue nation that may try to hold us hostage or blackmail our allies and friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure the education system fulfills its hope and promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had a strong record of working with Democrats and Republicans in Texas to make sure no child is left behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I understand the limited role of the federal government, but it could be a constructive role when it comes to reform, by insisting that there be a strong accountability systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My intentions are to earn your vote and earn your confidence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m asking for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want you to be on my team.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And for those of you working, thanks from the bottom of my heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For those of you making up your mind, I would be honored to have your support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank everybody who watched and listened tonight because this is indeed a crucial time in American history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’re at a fork in the road.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have this incredible prosperity, but a lot of people have been left behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we have a very important decision to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Will we use the prosperity to enrich all of our families and not just a few?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One important way of looking at this is to ask who are you going to fight for?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Throughout my career in public service, I have fought for the working men and women of this country, middle-class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Why?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because you are the ones who have the hardest time paying taxes, the hardest time making ends meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You are the ones who are making car payments and mortgage payments and doing right by your kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And a lot of times there are powerful forces that are against you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Make no mistake about it, they do have undue influence in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: and it makes a difference if you have a president who will fight for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know one thing about the position of president, it’s the only position in our Constitution that is filled by an individual who is given the responsibility to fight not just for one state or one district or the well-connected or wealthy, but to fight for all of the people, including especially those who most need somebody who will stand up and take on whatever powerful forces might stand in the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: There is a woman named Winifred Skinner here tonight from Iowa.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I mentioned her earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She’s 79 years old.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She has Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to cut her benefits or support any proposal that would.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She gets a small pension, but in order to pay for her prescription drug benefits, she has to go out seven days a week several hours a day picking up cans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She came all the way from Iowa in a Winnebago with her poodle in order attend here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to tell her, I’ll fight for a prescription drug benefit for all seniors and fight for the people of this country for a prosperity that benefits all.
